utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to you as well, Mr. Zlatkovic. Mr. Zlatkovic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony Monday. Then, Mr. Harvey, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, yesterday we finished at a point where I was asking you about KU 73/99, which you have at annex 7 to your statement. That's U0167557 in the Serbian original. Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you believe that the original documents in relation to this investigation would be in Jagodina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that certain information can be found in Jagodina. That's correct. What you asked me yesterday as to why I submitted a criminal complaint so late, I can tell you this: Everywhere in the world it is a well-established fact that when it comes to serious crimes it takes time. It can take from one to four years. I could have submitted a criminal complaint even five years after the crime once I gathered information that I needed about the perpetrators of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We were looking yesterday at the operation that you describe in paragraph 31 of your statement to push the KLA from the Djakovica-Pec road towards Jablanica. Would you agree, sir, that the Brahimaj family were part of the target of that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. Not only from the Djakovica-Pec-Decani, but also from the Djakovica-Glina-Pristina road. In just one week at Rakovina, the police members were attacked on that road eight to nine times. The terrorist groups kept provoking police forces and you can find this information in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were stationed in Rakovina during this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was stationed in Djakovica. On the 9th of August, I was present in Rastavica when the combat began.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, it's the 2nd of August that I'm focusing on particularly. Were you in Rastavica on the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Rastavica on the 2nd of August and on the 9th of August. I came there so as to be present and conduct an on-site investigation should any of the policemen be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you conduct any on-site investigation into the killing of a policeman on the 2nd of August in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't safe there because strong forces of Ramush Haradinaj and others were there in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The -- I just want to make sure that we're talking about the same operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Could we have, please, Defence exhibit -- or court exhibit D81 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: While that's coming up, sir, let me just explain, the document you're about to see is an order or a report, rather, on the combat tasks carried out on the 5th -- carried out by the 15th Armoured Brigade. And you'll see, sir, in the first paragraph there of the report it's written: "Between the 25th of July and the 6th of August, 1998, MUP units were engaged by decision of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija along the following axes ..." And then a number of different axes are recorded, and it's the last one that I want to draw your attention to. It's written in the English translation as Gradanica village. In fact, that should be Grabanice. Can you see where it says that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Grabavica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grabovica. I think it's Pecka Grabovica, it's near Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And can you -- you're actually looking at the Serb original. Does it not say "Grabanica"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have only heard of the village of Grabovica. It's possible that a village of Grabanica exists as well, I'm just not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And then the next point is Bandera trig 490, yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The next point is Glodjane village?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The next point is Jablanica village?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If -- in order just to clarify what we're looking at here --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If we could have displayed P10 now. Thank you. And if we could focus in the -- towards the top right-hand quarter of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you see -- first of all, can you see Jablanica there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And if you follow in a line from Jablanica almost directly -- if you were to draw a north-eastern line from Jablanica, do you see Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You see Bandera?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a stronghold of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Which one was? This whole area?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That whole area, especially Bandera. They had planted mines there on a number of occasions, killing policemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when mention is made of Gllogjan, which Gllogjan are we speaking about? Because there's Gllogjan which is the village where there is Mr. Haradinaj's house and there is another one, so I'm not quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, the witness is asked to look at the map. The Gllogjan where Mr. Haradinaj lives is not on the map at this moment, not visible. So therefore, where Mr. Harvey said "Jablanica" north-east could be only one Gllogjan, that is the Gllogjan between Grabanica and Jablanica. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And then if we follow that line again from Bandera we come to Grabanica. Do you see that? And following the line north-east: Jablanica-Glodjane-Bandera-Grabanica?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I appreciate it's a long time since you were involved in this operation, sir, but it was a very substantial MUP operation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was definitely a substantial MUP operation because that road had to be opened up, not only that road but the road leading towards Pristina as well. That's why it was done. As I told you yesterday and the day before, the terrorist forces from -- on both sides of the road were present and one couldn't travel on those roads. You can see it in the documents. A lot of civilians were killed on those roads, not just policemen, but civilians, soldiers, and I don't know who else. You can find it in the material the names of the people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Because if we go back to KU 73/99, the document in annex 7 to your statement where you recorded: "At about 1600 hours on the 2nd of August, the terrorist group led by Ramush Haradinaj and the other reported individuals which operated in the village of Jablanica ..." I'll miss out the next bit, "carried out a terrorist attack against members of Republic of Serbia MUP. On that occasion, the criminal terrorist group killed the policemen Zeljko Bozic, member of MUP, Pristina SUP." If one simply read that as it stands, it looks as if this is just a random attack on an individual policeman, doesn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how you read this, but this is standard terminology under Yugoslav law. We had received a report that in the Jablanica region in one of terrorist's operations, the policeman was killed. It is certain that the police force responded. Based on that I wrote a criminal complaint, or rather, a report which was sent to the regional public prosecutor in Pec, who was then supposed to take action based on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: What action was taken based on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no action was taken. The file was sent, and then the regional court and the prosecutor's office in Pec had to be relocated to Serbia to Leskovac, so no further action could be taken under those circumstances. This is why the file was sent here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: This was a major attempt to effectively wipe out the KLA in the Jablanica area, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only in Jablanica. In the entire area where there were units of the KLA. Let me tell you, it is not our fault that the constitution provided for that. Whenever there's a rebellion in any country not just in Serbia or Yugoslavia, you know what the state does, they use the police force, the army, they use whatever they can in order to quash the rebellion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, you're not accused at this moment. You're just asked whether there was a major attempt to effectively wipe out the KLA in the Jablanica area. No one says -- no one asks whether you were entitled to do that, but I think what is the matter on Mr. Harvey's mind might be that where in the report it seems or it looks as if there was just some terrorists attacking a policeman that Mr. Harvey, on the basis of these documents, seeks to establish whether this was just such an incident or whether there was a major operation going on which might shed a different light on the event. No one is questioning at this moment whether and on the basis of what you were entitled, but just to establish what were the circumstances in which the event took place that is described in this report. So there's no need for you to -- to justify or to defend. Just answer the questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your guidance. It wasn't just that the policeman who was killed participated in this operation; no, the entire unit participated but one policeman was killed. That's my response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to turn to what you discovered as a result of this operation and for those purposes could you have the brown folder in front of you, Mr. Zlatkovic, and it's 34A for you and 34B for non-B/C/S speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, this is the document that you've already looked at with Mr. Emmerson that's dated the 20th of August of 1998, and it begins -- it's the official note. If we look at the very first page in the Serbian original, U0169447, underneath the Tribunal number there, there is a handwritten number 541 of 98. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Can you enlighten us as to what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the number that this official note was registered under in the register, the one that I told you that existed in Jagodina. I don't know where the state security office is located now. I don't know whether it's in Jagodina or it's -- it could be Vranje, perhaps, and you can look it up there. But this is the number that the note was registered under. It means that the note exists. It was registered under this number in one of the register books, and you could look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that guidance. You see, I appreciate that you say you have not seen this document before it was shown to you by Mr. Dutertre this past Sunday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We suffer from the same difficulty. We didn't see it until Monday, but you say there is a register from which this document was taken that ought to be available for all of us to look at probably in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, the note reads: "Through our priority work on collecting information about S/C/Serbs and Montenegrins who have disappeared or been kidnapped, we have found out that the persons who were being detained in Jablanica and Glodjane during the last actions in these villages have been killed and thrown into a canal located above the village of Saptej that leads to Radonjicko Jezero lake." Again, I appreciate that you weren't the author of this document, but would you agree that written on the 20th of August where we see there: "During the last actions ..." Are we to interpret that during the last actions carried out by MUP and SUP in August and that that was the source of the information, the priority work on collecting information, that's where this information came from?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we see a number of references to intelligence information. I just want to ask you this, if you would turn, please, to the second page at the top in the Serb original there is -- it's the second paragraph on the second page. It says: "The RDB state security department centre was informed of the gist of the statement by dispatch number 529 of the 19th of August, 1998." First of all -- first of all, there isn't a question. If you just wait for the question, sir. The dispatch number 529, again is that another register number like the one that we saw at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- There might be some confusion. The original says "529." The English translation says "527." Let's first establish that. And then another matter is that the handwriting to which you referred at the very beginning is not appearing in the translation. It's just good for the record to know that the handwriting that's 541/98 and some other handwriting only appears on the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Your Honour, I was -- when I referred to 529, I'm looking at the top of page 2 of the document, not halfway down where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm sorry. I'm -- my eyes moved too quickly. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The gist of the statement, are we to deduce from that that a number of statements were taken from information sources and then they were condensed into a report giving the gist of the statement to the RDB?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely, and that is why such a dispatch was sent to the RDB, in order for them to take such actions as they were supposed to take because they were superior to the other services and must have been agreeing on the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, the statements to which this then refers, were they also -- was it also your practice to file those statements in a register or folder somewhere?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. As a rule this was registered in files. There are still such registers and can be found. Only those registers that perished in the bombardment cannot be found, but definitely the records exist and you can ask them to be produced to you. There is a register. You can, I'm sure, find the dispatch number 529, sent on such and such a date to the RDB in Prizren or Pec or wherever. I'm sure it must be there.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I want to come back to the 2nd of August and the actions carried out by MUP forces then. In the context of something you said on Monday, sir, at page 6913, line 1, of the transcript you said: "The police decided to settle accounts with the terrorists and uncover the perpetrators and free the people who had been kidnapped." I want to examine what you mean by the expression "settle accounts" in the context of the push towards Jabllanice. The units that made up the attack that was launched beginning on the 25th of July, as we have seen from the report from the 15th Armoured Brigade, did they include the special anti-terrorist unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They certainly did. Well, perhaps not the term to "settle accounts" perhaps does not reflect what I wanted to say. There was a great problem there. Eight or nine attacks had been launched over several days at the Rakovina check-point. Several policemen got killed there. The road was practically blocked. In the event of a policeman getting wounded, there was no way of taking him to the hospital. There were women there who were ill and who needed urgent medical treatment, there were women in labour. They should have been transported over to the Pristina hospital, but there was no way of doing that. There was constant fire, and that was the reason why it was decided to carry out the terrorist ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That was the reason it was decided to settle accounts, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Right. And the other units involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry, we had a bit of interference, let me just ask that question again. Was the Munja unit, M-u-n-j-a, involved?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. They had various names. I apologise for this. I think that the Munjas were from Djakovica, or rather, from Pec, and I had never been in touch with them. They were ordinary policemen, let me tell you. They merely underwent some training, some anti-terrorist training, but they were just ordinary men like all the others. It's only that they were given these names like Munja, so that they might be distinguishable in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You're suggesting that the Munja were just ordinary policemen? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. It was a unit composed of ordinary policemen. I don't know whether the Munja were from Djakovica or Pec, but they were ordinary policemen who simply accepted such burden upon their shoulders to carry in combat. They were mostly young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: They were hand-picked criminals, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Please. These men are active today. You are free to go and seek for them. You can go to Pec or Djakovica. You will find them active and working today. You will see that they are no criminals. They were men who were in the service, had been admitted into the service and undergone training before these events. Then the war broke out and they were young. They were willing to show what they had learnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: They were willing to commit war crimes, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that. That's what you are saying. I don't know who they committed war crimes against.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: They were led by a man called Mrvti, weren't they, M-r-v-t-i [sic]? My pronunciation might be a bit off.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you check it out in Pec through the Pec SUP. I don't know who this Mrtvi person is, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It's a nickname, it's not his actual name. It means "the dead," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite clear to me, the fact that this is his nickname. Maybe he styled himself that way or maybe that's what they called him since childhood, but you can check it out. I'm sure it's quite easy to check that out through the Pec MUP, whether he had been on the service, which schools he completed. I'm merely referring you to that, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, I think the question is rather simple: Are you aware of a man called - although not being his own name - Mrtvi, who led a certain unit. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I never heard of any such man. I heard of Munja but not of a person called Mrtvi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was another question put to you which I think was not clearly answered, perhaps also because of the way in which it was put to you. But were there any members of this unit, Munja, that had criminal records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they were admitted in the police, they must not have had any criminal records. Therefore, at the moment when they were admitted on to the police force, they certainly did not have any criminal records. I'm sure of that. Now, I don't know about what happened later on. I don't know whether they were amnestied in any way. What I'm sure of is that a person cannot be admitted into the police force if he has a criminal record. Such persons are normally vetted and that's all this is to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the normal situation, but perhaps in situation which are not quite normal, could it have happened that members of this unit were admitted despite perhaps the fact that they had criminal records? Are you aware of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The -- I gave you the name Mrtvi. Does the name Nebojsa Minic mean anything to you, because that I understand was the given name of that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's more like it. This person is some -- was arrested somewhere in Latin America and brought over to The Hague, I believe, to be held responsible for the crimes he committed. I read it somewhere in the papers. I can tell you that much, but I don't know the man and I don't know whether he, indeed, committed what he is charged with. But he wasn't in Djakovica, he was in Pec. What I told you is what I was able to read in the papers. I don't want to come across to you as a one-sided person. I really want to present the situation as it was on both sides and I want to tell the truth. And thank you for telling me this. This is the man. This is the name, the given name of that person, if he was extradited. I know that he was somewhere in Latin America.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: He was the head of that unit, wasn't he, Munja?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I'm not sure whether he was the head of the unit. He might have been at the head of the squad or something like that. He may have led a group to commit crimes. Everything is possible when there's a war on, but you are certainly on the right track now that you've given me the name because I have read in the papers that he is a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In the document I showed you earlier from the command of the 15th Armoured Brigade, reference is also made to the Brazil Unit. Are you aware of the Brazil Unit and what its job was?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never had any dealings with the army, believe me, never. I cannot tell you anything about the army. I was an operative, but I had nothing to do with the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, we better put that back on the screen, if we may, please, D00081, because this does not appear to be an army unit from what we see in the document. Now, if you would look, please, at the second full paragraph, the one at the top of the page that you have in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All right. Does it say: "The MUP forces engaged," and we're not talking about the VJ here, we're talking about "the MUP forces engaged consisted of the 1st and 2nd" --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the Brazil Unit. MUP, SAJ, and Brazil.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. You've read that over to yourself. Now, is it your testimony that the Brazil Unit was not a unit of police at all but was a VJ unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is the first time I hear of the Brazil Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Is it possible, do you believe, that a Brazil Unit could have existed within the MUP and you would have been unaware of it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about it and I really cannot tell you anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, two things. First of all, the same question has been put to the witness several times, and the way the question was phrased this last time was clearly of a speculative nature. So I would like to object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the question has been put, the question has been answered. Mr. Harvey, are you going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm not taking it any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then -- then there's no need at this moment to give a ruling on the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The job of those units between the 25th of July and the 6th of August in relation to Jablanica was, among other things, to seize any documents that could be helpful to the MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre. Before you answer the question, Witness, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The question is: "The job of those units..." Et cetera. What units are we talking about? Could Mr. Harvey tell us what units he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, several units have been mentioned. Could you please be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, I was referring back to that previous paragraph that I had just read from Defence Exhibit 81. I thought it was clear, but apparently not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your question would include all of the units mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All of the units engaged in this operation, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you'll repeat them for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: All of those units engaged in this operation against the KLA during that time-period, the 25th of July and the 6th of August, among their responsibilities was to try and obtain as many KLA-related documents as possible. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree with that, and to recover the dead bodies. There were stories of them being in Jablanica, Dasinovac, Volujak, Lake Radonjic. That was the objective of the operation, to obtain the information because the attacks were happening all the time and that was why the action was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey -- And you, Mr. Zlatkovic, I take it that when you are talking about the tasks or -- of these units, that you do not include the Brazil Unit of which you just testified you were not aware of its existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I'm speaking of the ordinary police force, the SAJ, and of nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, that's the reason why I granted the objection that it's very difficult to ask a witness what were the tasks of a unit he just testified he doesn't know of. So therefore I took it that the answer mainly focused on what the -- what the aims were of the units participating to the extent this witness knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And that was the question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The -- you had information before the 2nd of August or before the 25th of July, indicating that there might be bodies in Jabllanice, is that correct, from your last answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jablanica was a tough nut, because according to the stories when I arrived there in 1997 to deal with homicides, policemen told me of this village that they had never entered the village for seven or eight years, that they had entered the village once and were driven out. It was common sense telling us that something was going there. There was no law enforcement there. The police force could not have any -- could not gain any access to that area, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I understand that point exactly, but that meant the only way you could find out anything about what was happening in Jablanica was from people who became informants to the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In addition to that gentleman, you recall I mentioned the name of a witness to you yesterday who has already testified to this Tribunal, and we give him the number Witness 6, and you indicated to us that from his actual name you were able to deduce that he was probably a Catholic Albanian. Do you recall that, Witness? I see you nodding your head? If you could --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall you saying that yesterday. Other than that, I never saw the man. It is quite possible that I read in the material earlier on that his son had been killed. He was in Jablanica for some time. Then a delegation was sent, he was at the head of the delegation from Jablanica, asking that he be released. This was in the statement by Bekim Kalamashi. Most probably his son was released later on, if that's what you're referring to. I never saw this Catholic in my life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, I understood from you yesterday that you knew nothing about this man at all, but now it appears that you do have quite a bit of information about him.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not put a specific-enough question to me. Had you asked me whether this man's son had been kidnapped - and I am still not claiming that - I would have given you the same reply I gave you today. I worked on that material and I know that one man from Batosane [phoen], either a young man or just a man, was kidnapped, was held in Jablanica for a while. Bekim Kalamashi told us this. Then a delegation went there, the delegation that he had allegedly seen as they travelled through Crmljane, asking that he be released from prison. They did not release him, and later on he allegedly heard that the man had been released. Now, I don't know whether it's the same man. Had you asked me this yesterday, I would have replied.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think we need a redaction at page 19, it's just come off my screen, line 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Would you please prepare that redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Page 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, yesterday you said you would not need less than half an hour. I interpret that in my own way that is perhaps 40 minutes, 45 minutes, otherwise you should have said not less than an hour. The witness has to travel rather soon. So therefore you've now taken 50 minutes and I'd like you to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- I will have two more questions, if I may. Your Honour has already noted that a number of the witness's answers have been lengthy and not necessarily responsive. I'm doing my best to keep within bounds but I do apologize for having gone over what I had anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: When the MUP and SUP forces entered Jabllanice, are you aware that they not only seized documents on the 2nd of August, they also set fire to homes, in fact destroying some 100 houses in Jabllanice on that date. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were listening on the radio to communications. Are you saying you were completely unaware of any documents being seized from Jabllanice, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have some documents that are part of evidence here. Now, whether they come from Jablanica or Babaloc, I really don't know that. The documents were found about the command, the military establishment, and some other matters. Let me tell you, nobody's going to announce over radio, We are setting houses on fire. No. They normally say, We have been attacked. We are pulling out. You know what people normally say when they are in the army and in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to conduct an investigation into the killing of the mother and grandmother of Lahi Brahimaj, who were hacked to death on that occasion on the 2nd of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I was not informed about that. But if that is true, I am shocked to hear that. I fully condemn that. All I was asked to do was to find the perpetrators of the crime in Decani where four people were killed. I did that very quickly in a course of a couple of days, arresting Dragan Jovanovic, a policeman, who was sentenced, who was on trial in Pec and in Leskovac. I have trouble because I testified --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We're short of time and your answer to my question is simply: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Dutertre, the witness is supposed to leave in approximately ten minutes. Could you please be as efficient as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. There were many questions I wanted to put to the witness, but I'll only deal with the most significant issues, and as a result I will not necessarily adopt a chronological or logical order in my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zlatkovic, page 6940 of the transcript yesterday you seemed to be saying that there was a Serb check-point in Rznic from the 12th of August to the -- until the Serb offensive in September. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you go yourself to that check-point in Rznic, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go to the check-point. I went a couple of times to Prilep. In front of a mosque there there was a check-point where some policemen had been killed, so that's where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Fine. How do you know that this check-point in Rznic remained there after the 12th of August in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard that on the radio communication. It was also discussed in meetings, that that check-point was constantly under attack. The policemen kept complaining because fire was opened from mortars on the check-point, and I think that even some people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'd like to read out a report by the European Commission Monitoring Mission dated 19th of August, and I'd like to ask your comments about this. This document has been tendered and admitted. The MFI number is as follows: 311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst the documented is being brought up, can I seek an assurance that this is an issue that arises out of cross-examination because I don't recall this document having being referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me that one of the witnesses commented or gave some comments about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In re-examination you're supposed to limit yourself to what had been raised in cross-examination, because otherwise you should have raised it in the examination-in-chief. That's what Mr. Emmerson is telling us, and it's not that in re-examination that you -- everything is open to you to revisit what has been visited by another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but the witness has been put many questions about the check-point at Rznic during cross-examination, and I believe that with this document we can shed some light on the -- what is stated about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read, then let's see what happens. Let's also not lose time. Is it on the screen now, the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. It's a document dated 19th of August, 1998. I would like to have a look at paragraph 3, we could scroll down a bit maybe and the last sentences are as follows: [In English] "There is evidence to suggest that UCK has already slipped back into the ruins of the villages taken by Serb security forces last weekend principally Lodza, Rausic, and Rznic. This has led to fears that the Serb security forces would recommence their offensive this coming week." [Interpretation] Mr. Zlatkovic, can you comment on this document, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, actually not that I think, it is a fact that immediately after that they withdrew. First the farmers, the elderly men came and some children who were there with cattle, whereas in fact those were the people who informed the KLA about the movements of Serb forces. They came to that area and then they started targeting the check-point in Rznic, targeting from mortars and rocket-launchers, the hand-held ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, in your statement you mentioned the second operation that took place in September, paragraph 33 up until paragraph 43 of your statement. And I would like us to have a look at paragraph 43 in particular where you state that a check-point was set up in Rznic and Prilep. Why was a check-point or check-points set up in Rznic and Prilep if there had still been a check-point in Rznic since the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA forces kept attacking non-stop, and that's why the road was important. People needed to receive food-supplies because people living in that town had no more food and the road had to be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Yes, but I was wondering about the meaning of re-establishing a check-point in Rznic during the September offensive if the check-point had been set up on the 12th of August had remained there the entire time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They strengthened the check-point precisely for those reasons. The winter was approaching and the population needed to receive supplies. One didn't know when they were going to take up that territory again because they started coming back, started receiving reinforcements and attacking. There was rumour that the OSCE was supposed to come, that the police was supposed to withdraw from all check-points, and this is why it was set up in this way. We started creating multi-ethnic police force at the time. Albanians were members of it, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness now goes in details you're not seeking. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let me move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: At page 6911 of the transcript yesterday, lines 16 to 25, and page 6912, lines 1 to 8, Mr. Emmerson put questions to you about one of the attacks led against one of the MUP units on the 9th of August next to Glodjane, a MUP unit that was conducting regular assignments. That's what you stated. Mr. Emmerson tried to clarify what you meant by "regular assignments," and you stated that it was a regular unit. I'd like things to be very clear. Do you mean that the offensive led on the 9th of August towards Glodjane by the -- that MUP unit or on that MUP unit was directed against a regular unit because it was not an uncontrolled unit and because it was a unit that was there officially or do you mean that it was a unit that would regularly patrol the Glodjane area?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I was going to say is that that unit was supposed to perform regular patrols, not only in Glodjane, Babaloc, the village of Dubrava and some other villages in the area. I can't remember their names. Let me tell you, this was the territory of Serbia and, naturally, police had to enter and be able to enter all settlements in case there was a problem with law and order and there was a problem with law and order because they had started digging trenches, wearing -- bearing weapons and carrying mortars and so on, firing at peaceful citizens and so on, that's why the police wanted to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Are you aware that at some point the police station of Rznic was closed down?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the impact of the closure of the Rznic police station on patrols, did it have an impact on the way patrols could be conducted in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This station was closed down after Otovic was killed, and the terrorists moved into the station after that. Since there were reports from citizens, an electrician reported that he had been mistreated by some people, he was unable to do his work. And as a result, the police wanted to maintain law and order in that area, but for the well-known reasons it was impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, if you would please listen carefully to the question. The question was: What was the impact on patrolling after they had left, not why they had to leave but what was the impact on patrolling the area after the police station was closed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I'm not sure I quite understand what you say. What impact ensued? Well, the impact was that the police was unable to enter the territory because it was under the control of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Let me move on to another topic, and that is the involvement of the army in the 11th of August operation. Page 6920 at 69 -- to 6922 of the transcript, Mr. Zlatkovic, you were asked about what you knew about the involvement of the army in that particular offensive of August -- in August, and you stated that you did not see any military personnel at page 6920 of the transcript. And you also stated that you were not aware of the involvement of the army, and that's to be found at page 6922 of the transcript. Please let me put my questions before answering. At paragraphs 36 of your statement, you said that you were in Rastavica during the offensive and that you were listening to what was going on on the police radio. Listening to the conversations of your police colleagues who were taking part in fightings around Glodjane and in that area -- did you hear anything, listening to these conversations, did you hear anything indicating that the infantry was present around Glodjane and Gramocelj?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, I asked the witness at the time: "You emphasised and you made clear a distinction between what you saw and what you perhaps learned ... " and then I asked him whether in these days whether he was aware of the army being involved in the operations. I mean you could ask him whether he had not heard it by telephone, that he did not receive a Telefax on it. That answer is clear. There's no reason to revisit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise to my feet but in this context the witness was asked and answered to the effect that between the 9th and the 11th of August, he himself entered the territory to conduct on-site investigations into each of the incidents he reported.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on. That's all on the record, now. Mr. Dutertre, the witness has to leave so would you please put your last question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, yesterday you talked about the loyal Albanians. Do you know if some of these loyal Albanians were reported missing during that period of March to September 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those people who disappeared were mostly the ones who were loyal people or perhaps there could have been some feuds between them. But normally those were peaceful, law-abiding citizens who paid taxes and did everything they were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Is there any need for further questions? Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have very few, very short questions, Mr. Zlatkovic, and I'd like you to answer them as short as possible. In your statement although not in the portion that is admitted into evidence, you say you believe that 124 cartridges were found at the Lake Radonjic area. There is no report at that part of your statement as an annex sourcing this. What made you believe that there were 124?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure that it is contained in the report, the figure of 124 cartridges. Perhaps there were more than that, but the technicians gathered 124 cartridges and they took it to the institute for ballistic expertise in Pristina. Stojan - I don't remember his last name - analysed this. I'm sure that that fact exists in the report or in the documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Even the cartridges from Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that this was the operation covering Dasinovac and the Lake Radonjic canal area. So I do understand that your recollection stems from the report made on cartridges found during that investigation.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one question about something you said earlier today. I'll just find it. You said you were not aware of any person by the name of Mrtvi, I think you said, as a leader of a certain unit. You said you didn't know that name. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, when I heard the nickname from counsel, that I didn't know that nickname. But once counsel mentioned the given name, then I remembered that I read in the papers that that man had been captured somewhere in Argentina or Brazil or somewhere. I knew the given name because that was the name mentioned in papers, and he was apparently implicated in some crimes. Now, whether that's true or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, you testified at that moment: "This is the name, the given name," of that person, which suggests that hearing this given name, that you link that to a name you were aware of, whereas you earlier testified that you didn't know about that name. That surprised me. Do you have an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read all that in the papers once he was captured, either in Brazil or I don't know where, and it was then that I remembered. During combat I really knew nothing about him. Now, when this happened, when he was captured, the papers kept writing about him for several days, his photograph was in the papers and I wanted to tell the Court that I learned about that from the papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Then also learned about the name Mrtvi; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the papers, the nickname Mrtvi was also mentioned, and there were photographs of him in a uniform with other people. It was in the papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I understand. I have no further questions for you. The only thing, I have to apologise, in an earlier question I put to you, I think it was on Monday, I suggested that you had testified about two houses where the police had sought shelter in the -- on the 24th of March. That was incorrect because your testimony clearly was that there was one house where you sought shelter, so I -- to the extent I confused you at that moment, I apologise for that. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need to apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no further questions. You are excused, Mr. Zlatkovic. I'd like to thank you, although I'll do it very quickly, for coming to The Hague and answering all the questions. And I sincerely hope that, although we went some ten minutes over the scheduled time that you'll be in time at the airport and have a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Zlatkovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to thank Your Honours and the Prosecution and all who assisted me, as well as Defence counsel, for inviting me to come here and state what I know. I stated what I know in a most correct way. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One thing slipped out of my mind, Mr. Guy-Smith, and that is that I more or less promised Mr. Dutertre that he would be aware of annex 10 when starting re-examination, and we are still waiting for an answer. I should have done it. Nevertheless, I'd like to hear that answer anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We have discussed annex 10 amongst ourselves, and we are -- although I had taken the initial position that on behalf of the Balaj Defence we objected to the annex in toto for the reasons stated. Concerning the manner in which the annex was used, there is one portion of the annex which we object to now, and that is the portion that deals with reference to ballistic reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, that objection, would you agree? Would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need to read through this particular portion. I would need to know what the nature of the objection is in relation to that particular excerpt. Could Mr. Guy-Smith be more specific? I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, if you would have an -- a possibility to help us out. Let me just see now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the English version, I have it as page 2, it's 0188-2451 is the ERN number. There -- it starts with the word in bold caps -- excuse me, in caps: "Attachment," and then it says: "Official dispatch of authorised official" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that on page 2 of the English you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's on page 2 of the English as I have it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I assist?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, and we've been trying to trace this through, I think the position, essentially, is that there is an error in the translation in the English, in the sense that the English translation skips two pages. And it's possible to see that as between the English translation for page 2349, which then skips to 2453. I've given -- yes. Your Honour will have an English translation that runs to 15 pages, I believe, and page 15 begins 2439 to 2450, does Your Honour have that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if you look to the next page of translation, it begins 2453 with a document headed: "Attachment 1.2" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, let me just have a look. That one starts 2451 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ah, Your Honour has that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Starting with the words: "Attachment 1.2" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see on this -- I have got two annexes 10, as a matter of fact, and one is complete and one is not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, you see, I have all versions available. There I see: "Official dispatch of authorised official Nebojsa Avramovic recorded under PU1422/98 of the 4th of December and then four ballistic reports are mentioned."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's where your objection goes to?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, is that clear to you now? That is the attached -- I don't know whether they are attached to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, they're not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They're not attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, the mere reference to attached reports which are not attached, that's where the objection goes?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to speak across Mr. Guy-Smith, but there are three preceding paragraphs which ultimately seek to do much the same as Mr. Avramovic sought to do in his witness statement, namely to summarize what the conclusions of the disputed ballistics evidence was understood to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- And it culminates in a reference to those four reports, none of which are either attached or available. And as Your Honours will recall on the last occasion, the position taken by the Trial Chamber was that the admissibility of the forensics evidence, the ballistic comparison, was a matter to be determined in due course in respect of the calling of the ballistic witness himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the Chamber suggested to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And further pleadings are due in next week in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that is attached at annex 10, as I see it here in Serbian, stops at page 2450 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you -- if the parties could please sort out this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- And see on what version what objections are made and what -- whether there's any opposition from the Prosecution. Then the Chamber would like to hear -- but I do see that the focus is on the -- the presentation of the results of ballistic evidence, ballistic investigations, and that -- that seems not to be the focus of the annex 10 as a whole. It's just a certain element in it where the Defence takes issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, Mr. President, one last point about the annexes. In annex 5, I discovered an error similar to the one you identified in annex 4 with relation to a reasonable doubt or reasonable ground. This has been corrected now and the document has been sent or filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it then that the correct document has been uploaded and that the Defence has been informed about the matter, Mr. Dutertre?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just been told that the document has not been uploaded yet, but it -- that should happen very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You will provide a copy to the -- to the Defence so that they are aware of this change. Then before we have a break, for the next witness, the next witness which -- who will testify through a videolink, protective measures were asked for. The Chamber understood that the Legal Officers of the Chamber had been informed by the Defence that there were no objections to grant the protective measures as sought. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that the reasons to follow that the Chamber decides that for the next witness to be heard through videolink, that face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym are granted, and the registrar -- yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, and I don't know how the -- how the Chamber or the Prosecution wishes to handle the matter. Considering the nature of the testimony that I think is going to be adduced with regard to this witness, we may well be in private session for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wherever there's need to go into private session on the basis of the substance of the testimony which might identify him, of course special caution is asked for the Prosecution and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Based on where I believe this testimony is going, it would directly affect other witnesses who previously had been granted anonymity of some form or fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is, of course -- Mr. Dutertre, I don't know whether it's you who is going to take the next witness or Mr. Re. I can imagine that from what the Chamber expects will be the substance of the testimony, we have seen that there is a 92 ter statement for this witness, that much of it could not be easily elicited in open session without violating protective measures granted in respect of another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are quite aware of it, we have considered it, and we will take all necessary precautions during the testimony to ensure that the full protective measures are -- full efficacy is given to the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In this respect, I further would like to ask your attention for the following. I do understand that another witness for which the Prosecution has considered whether or not to hear testimony through videolink, but who will now be a 92 bis witness, that the protective measures granted to that witness -- for that witness pre-trial might not be fully sufficient. And therefore, if you are going to submit the 92 bis statement, that your special attention is asked for any application for further protective measures for the trial stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will do that. It may be that we submit two, a redacted and an unredacted version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break, and after the break we'll continue with a -- we'll start -- it will be open session, but we need 30 minutes to prepare for the videolink. So therefore, we'll resume at ten minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever confusion, although the courtroom looks as if we are in private session, we are not. Nevertheless, the screens are down since on the computer screens of the parties one sees the undistorted view of the witness who will testify and the public should not view that. So therefore, the public at this moment is limited to the screens and not a direct view of the Chamber, but nevertheless, we are not in closed session. The next witness, Mr. Re, will be Witness 56?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who will testify through a videolink, and I do understand that Witness 56 is a 92 ter witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now before we start, the Chamber has received a 92 ter statement. The Chamber has also received I think four objections from the Balaj Defence but is aware that further discussions have taken place. Mr. Guy-Smith, is there anything remaining from the objections, apart from --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct. Further discussions have been had and we also received an e-mail from Mr. Re with regard to our objections. It's our understanding with regard to the objections contained in paragraphs 5, 15, and 16, this information will be led and further enhanced, therefore, the problem will not exist. With regard to paragraph 9, the issue is simply with regard to the definition of understand, and if we are using "understand" to mean, which I believe that we are, an information was related to this witness and based on the information that this witness obtained he is making certain assertions, then we have no difficulties, as opposed to "understand" being a conclusion. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If a witness can testify about what came into his mind when he heard a certain story, that is interpreting what someone tells you. If someone tells me that he drove very fast with his car, I would understand that as to be certainly a speed above 25, 30, 40 kilometres. That is, you can testify about what came into your mind, which is a matter of fact, whether that is correct or not might depend on whether we're talking about a real car or about a toy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't think so that's where -- I don't think that's where my concern lies and I would agree with you if you take the same hypothetical and the issue is I understand that the individual driving the car was speeding or violating the traffic laws, I would take issue with the issue of understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because there are too many other component parts that are involved in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever the matter is, the Chamber of course has considered it having looked at and the Chamber does not find this part of the statement to be inadmissible. Of course, I can understand that you would like to further explore perhaps in cross-examination that part to better understand to use the wrong word what the witness at that time understood, but it's not a matter of non-admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We maintain our position --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- We maintain our position with regard to it being a legal conclusion which is inappropriate for this witness to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very briefly --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise. Part of the reason so the Chamber understands my concern is that by virtue of the manner of this presentation of evidence - and that I mean the 92 ter statement - there is an aspect of leading that occurs that otherwise would not necessarily occur. And the difficulty that I think that is presented oftentimes - and I won't belabour the point - but the difficulties presented oftentimes is that where you have a written statement, the information quite frankly, is leading. And we see what happens with regard to witnesses when they testified viva voce they oftentimes do not, as we would say, come up to proof as opposed to what is being said in their written statements. It is for that reason that I'm concerned about it where you have such a thing as a legal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that. Whether it's a legal conclusion or whether of course some words have both a legal meaning and a factual meaning, therefore -- but as I said before, the Chamber does not exclude this portion of paragraph 9 from admission on the basis of your objections but of course I have not heard any other objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I have nothing to add to that. I simply wanted to clarify to make absolutely certain that we're all working from the same documents, that Your Honours have an original statement taken on the 29th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 29th of May, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- together with a further statement of the 10th of July which amends the 29th of May statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and therefore for my purposes, I've simply struck through the words that the witness seeks to amend in the earlier statement so as to remove --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I must admit -- I am aware of the two. I am just looking at the second one --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 of the second statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- seeks to essentially delete --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- delete a portion of paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wondered whether they had any impact on paragraph 9, but it has not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is fully aware that there is a correction more or less in the July 2007 statement to the 29th of May 2006 statement. Mr. Re, are you--

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are. Just to clarify in relation to there being any misunderstanding about what Mr. Guy-Smith's understanding is. He said it is our understanding with regard to the objections the information will be led and further the problem will not exist. The communication we had is that -- we intend to tender the statement and ask further clarifying questions from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well the decision of the Chamber anyhow is that it's not excluded from admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then do we have at this moment a connection with Pristina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a videolink with Pristina at this moment. In Pristina Witness 56 is present, but before we address Witness 56, could the representative of the registry confirm that there is a videolink which works well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Good morning, Mr. President, good morning Judges. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not hear at this moment. Could you please repeat it, I couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I now --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Judges, good morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now hear you well. Is both the audio and video working well in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Yes, it is working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to address the witness. Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. We're not getting any transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not getting it on audio? Not video, not audio? You have to put the Elmo button to get it on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have video but very weak audio, hardly any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have to adjust the volume. Just -- we again try the audio -- Madam Registrar, would you please say a few words.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Good morning again, Mr. President. How are things in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just checking now whether Defence counsel can hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is just about audible. There is a very high level of interference but it is just about audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be any problem also a problem for the interpreters and the transcribers then -- but perhaps Madam Registrar in Pristina is a bit far away from the microphone. Could you please come a bit closer to the microphone and see whether it's any better.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] So, Your Honour, can you hear me better now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, still the quality of the audio is rather poor. Is there any way the technicians could assist us in improving the audio quality and could you speak another few words, Madam Registrar, in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Here we can do something with the volume. We are checking right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the quality now has far improved.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] It's getting better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you speak another few words and just see whether the court reporter is now better able to hear you. I do understand that the court -- the transcriber receives the sound now from Pristina in an acceptable quality but the sound from this courtroom isn't reaching her. Could the technicians assist in having this fixed as well. So it would be me now who would have to continue to speak rather than Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that one of the problems is that using the proper channels that Madam Registrar in Pristina now is also on the Albanian channel rather than on the English channel. That causes some problems. Let's proceed and see how it works. Witness 56, can you see me and can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can't hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't hear you. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is to some extent a surprising answer because I asked whether you could hear me. Let's go step by step. Can you see me on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have no problem at all. I know what happened to me, and nothing else than what happened to me at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but let me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may write what you want, but I know what happened with my sons and I was not allowed to speak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take me wherever you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to take you wherever I want. I just wanted first to verify whether you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what you are saying. I know what happened to me in 1986 -- 1998, that they took my son, and then they brought him back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was at 1.00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second. I first want to be sure that you can hear my voice in a language you understand. Can you or can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then at -- we'll soon come to the point where we would like to hear what you have to tell us. Would you please not speak when I'm speaking because that's very difficult for the interpreters. The first thing we'll have to do is after I have established that you can see me and that you can hear me, that you give a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The -- so therefore, I would like you to repeat these words in your own language, since I do understand that you have difficulties in reading I'll just tell you. Would you please repeat the following words: I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you what happened to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing other than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, we'll come to that very soon, but there is a rule which says that if a witness tells his story, he first has to give a solemn declaration so I am seeking your cooperation in order to make you -- have you making that solemn declaration. And I invite you to repeat the words I speak to you and then we'll come later to your story. So first would you repeat: I solemnly declare ... Could you please repeat those words: I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what you are saying to me, solemnly, what is this solemnly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I am inviting --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you that on the 11th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. One second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came and took my son --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and I know nothing other than that, and I know no one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second --
