utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will wait for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, I'll explain to you. I'll first tell you what solemn declaration we would like to hear from you because you have to give such a solemn declaration before you tell your story. I'll later ask you to repeat it, but what I'm going to invite you to do is to give a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. But you have to speak those words before you tell us what happened and before you answer any questions that will be put to you, and those questions later will be about the events you already started to talk to us about. So therefore, could you please repeat the words I now speak to you, the meaning of those words being that you'll tell us the truth. So could you please repeat the following lines: I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I speak? Can I? Look here, whatever I know I have said, what happened to me in 1998 when they took my son and his wife and I don't know where they took them. They were four or five people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, Witness 56, we'd very much --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then they brought them back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are going to deal --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing other than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, and we are going to hear that from you, but before we do so, we first need you to confirm that you will speak the truth and the whole truth and nothing but the truth. That's a procedural rule. That's a rule of procedure which applies, and you first will have to give that solemn declaration; and then after that we'll ask you who you are, what happened -- at least Mr. Re will do so. So therefore, first would you please repeat my words because only after you have repeated them we can hear all the things you want to tell us. So therefore, I try it again. Would you please repeat the following words: I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other words to tell you. I know nothing other than what I've already said. I went to my staff and then informed them, and then two people came, two commanders came to my house, but they didn't allow me to speak at all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know more than what happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other words to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, we would like to hear what you are telling us as a witness, as a witness in a courtroom. And a witness in a courtroom, before he answers any questions, before he answers any questions - and I do understand that you can't say anything more than perhaps you know or that you have told already - but before we can hear your answers to the questions, you first have to make a solemn declaration that all your answers will be truthful. And therefore, it's for that reason that before we put questions to you that I'd like you to repeat my words, because then we can continue and then we can hear what you have to tell us. So therefore I invite you again, prior to the substance of your testimony, first to confirm that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So therefore, could you please repeat the following words: I solemnly declare ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I already told you, only those words I want to repeat now. They took my son and his wife at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who else is in the room, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Your Honour, we have an interpreter here ready to explain the witness this procedure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the witness was speaking to the interpreter who is present. Now I'll take a different approach. Witness 56, we will put questions to you later, but I first want to know from you if questions will be put questions to you later. But I first want to know from you if questions that we put to you, and if you give answers, are you going to tell us the truth. Could you please answer that with a yes or a no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already told the truth about what happened to me. I know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And whatever you will say today, that will be the -- whatever -- whatever you will say today, that will be the truth as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I already told you is the truth; namely, that they took them away and what they did I don't know, and then they brought them back home. And then after that I went to the headquarters and informed them of what happened. And then these two people came to my house and took notes. They didn't allow me to speak. And I didn't know the commander, I didn't know anyone. This is what I want to tell you what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I do understand that that's what you want to tell us. We might have quite some questions about it, but before we can put those questions to you, I'd like to know from you, as you said, you earlier told the truth, I take it that today you will tell us while answering questions you will tell us the truth as well, isn't it? Could you please answer that with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you I don't know Togeri. I know no one. They were dressed in the same way. I don't know Toger at all. Only when I saw him in The Hague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I told you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, Witness 56, I'll now try to explain to you what the procedure today will be. I do understand that you want to tell us what you've told already before -- please listen to me and wait for a second. Now, in a courtroom the procedure is as follows. First you are confirming that you will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, that's the first stage. Then after that, specific questions will be put to you where reference will be made most likely to what you already told before and what is on paper and some additional questions as well. And then after that this will conclude your testimony, but we cannot --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing else to tell you, sir. I'm sick. I'm 75 years old. I'm not feeling well. I'm disabled. You can do what you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing more than that. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chambers suggests, but would like to hear from the parties, if they would disagree that Madam Registrar in Pristina takes, at a quiet moment now during a short break, takes the opportunity to explain to the witness what I apparently am not able to explain in a way which seems to have any effect. Therefore, the suggestion is -- Madam Registrar in Pristina, you have understood what I said; that we have a break for approximately ten minutes, that again the procedure is explained to the witness and that we'll then see whether we can make any progress after that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Initially if that is the procedure that's going to be used, I would ask that that conversation be recorded or memorialised so that we can make sure that we are all fully cognizant of what transpired during that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other submissions by the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking for that is so that the Chamber is in a position to assure itself that any issues concerning competence or understanding of what the procedure is before any testimony is taken is memorialised in such a fashion that we don't have any doubts about that, because it is, in fact, the predicate before a witness can testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, your request is denied. Madam Registrar in Pristina is instructed to explain the procedure, what is expected from the witness, and not to touch upon any substance of the testimony. Madam Registrar is not a party and it is -- this is, although very transparent that it takes place, is just preparing the witness from a neutral person in order to be able to receive his testimony. Madam Registrar, the line in English is not very clear, but I can see your face. Have you understood my instructions well? If you would nod yes, that would be visible from here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [In Pristina] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We even understood that you said "yes, Your Honour." Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So all parties are clear, I implicitly trust the registrar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't understand your words to be of any doubt in that respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I hope there is some way that we can have some form of memorialisation of this because I think what is going to occur it is going to be some give-and-take in conversation as between a potential witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. If there is any reason at any later stage to get information from Madam Registrar in Pristina, we'll hear the reasons why that's necessary at that point in time. And of course, I have no doubts knowing Madam Registrar in Pristina that her memory serves her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I officially make the request and I think it goes directly to the issue of the competence that we may be -- of this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- the competence of him to testify, understand the proceedings and it also directly relates to the issue of the 92 ter submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break until -- yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just very briefly. In relation to the oath itself or the solemn declaration, I just draw Your Honours' attention to Rule 90(A), and of course Your Honour the Presiding Judge is reading from it. In our submission, although the words -- there is a -- a declaration is actually prescribed there: "I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth," and the witness is supposed to make the following declaration, in our submission for the purposes of the proceedings and the spirit and literal meaning of the declaration, it would be sufficient, as Your Honour tried I think, just for the witness to say, if asked, something along the lines of: We're going to ask you some questions; do you promise to tell the truth or just something like that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I already tried to not be formalistic, some would say unduly formalistic. Others would say that it would be my duty to be formalistic, but I approached the matter in both ways until now. Madam Registrar -- Witness 56, we'll disconnect for the time being and Madam Registrar will explain to you how we will proceed and at what moment you can tell your story. But we'll take a break of ten minutes and we'd like to see you back after these ten minutes. We stand adjourned until five minutes past 12.00. --- Break taken at 11.54 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before we proceed, I notice that Mr. Re made some submissions on the procedure just before we rose, to which there was no Defence response --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll not give that any follow-up until the Defence has had an opportunity to respond to that. Witness 56, again, can you see me, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 56, the Chamber would like to hear from you whether you promise that when answering questions whether you promise that you'll speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I'm telling you, the truth, what happened to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything that happened to me, I told you the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what you are going to tell us will be the truth then as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything, the truth, mine is the truth. There is no other truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber intends to proceed on the basis of what the witness just told us. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is understood. I would like to interpose for the record my concern about what has transpired for approximately, if the transcript is correct, 17 minutes with regard to a discussion which was, as I understood it, an explanation of the solemn declaration. I understand that there was a technical ability to memorialise the conversation. I understand there was a technical ability to videotape the conversation. And I watched a fair amount of it in which I saw what seemed to me - and it's my interpretation from the body language and the movement of the bodies and arms - a spirited and heated conversation between Witness 56 and the interpreter. I don't -- I also believe there was a telephone conversation between the registrar in Pristina and Legal Officer here concerning what occurred, but since we have no memorialisation of it, we don't know whether -- excuse me, whether or not the conversation was confined to the issue of the solemn declaration or, indeed, whether or not, as he has previously done already today, Witness 56 made other factual statements concerning the subject matter of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We need to have this memorialised because it could become -- it could become an issue -- it could become an issue with regard to Article 21, fair trial rights; it could become an issue with regard to cross-examination; it could become an issue with regard to credibility; it could become an issue with regard to bias. And the failure to have a memorialised record of what happened, what transpired in the 17 minutes I vigorously object to, especially in light of the fact that there was a technical way to have it taken care of without detriment to any party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the record, Mr. Guy-Smith. Ms. Gustafson, as I said before, the Chamber is willing to proceed not in any way to anticipate on what will happen but is willing to proceed with the examination-in-chief of the witness. It is suggested to you that in view of the experience we had until now that perhaps first, before putting specific questions to the witness, that the witness is invited to tell us what he wants to tell and then to go to more specific questions. Witness 56, we will proceed, and it will be Ms. Gustafson who will now put questions to you. Would you please carefully listen to the questions put to you by Ms. Gustafson and then answer them. Ms. Gustafson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait and hear what questions will be put to you, Witness 56, and please answer them. If you would look at your screen you will most likely see Ms. Gustafson in a second, who will address you. Ms. Gustafson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can the camera show Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 56.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could briefly go into private session in order to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Witness 56 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. For the public, I give the following information. We heard the testimony of Witness 56 through a videolink with protective measures. The Chamber would not be surprised if in the near future the parties would like to make submissions on to what extent the evidence given is admissible evidence and to what extent it will assist the Chamber in making any determinations in this case. The parties are informed that tomorrow we'll not start at 9.00. We'll start at 10.30. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, could we go into, I believe, closed session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In relation to the witness who just testified by videolink, Witness 56, our submission would be -- I'm not talking about the ultimate submission, just about the private nature of the testimony. Our submission -- preliminary submission is 95 per cent of it probably could be made public. I take it the Trial Chamber would invite the parties to submit to the Trial Chamber those parts which should be redacted. We could do that very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the parties are even invited to agree upon it so that we don't have to receive four submissions, but if the parties could agree one submission would do. And, of course, it is important perhaps also in view of what still might happen in relation to this witness that the public will have an idea on how the testimony was given, how it was received, what happened during the session because the trial should be public. We adjourn until tomorrow morning, 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of July, 2007, at 10.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
